building.local_amendments_note: Virginia's statewide code supersedes local building codes (Code of Virginia § 36-98, quoted in the state pack), so Richmond has no building or plumbing code amendments of its own. The city's Permits and Inspections page carries its own table, 'Building Codes for Richmond, Virginia', which lists only the 2021 Virginia editions and referenced standards, plus local structural design values (frost depth, wind speed, snow load, seismic category) that are design inputs, not amendments. Chapter 5 of the Richmond City Code (Municode) could not be read: Municode blocks automated access (HTTP 403).

fixtures.basis: Virginia's Uniform Statewide Building Code supersedes the building codes and regulations of cities (Code of Virginia § 36-98, quoted in the state pack from law.lis.virginia.gov), so Richmond cannot amend the toilet-count table or its rules. Richmond's own code table lists the 2021 Virginia Plumbing Code with no local edition, and nothing on its permit pages or in its commercial plan review guide changes the counts. The state pack's worked examples stand.

permit.required_quote: A. Section 108.1 When applications are required. Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities [...] 1. Construction or demolition of a building or structure. Installations or alterations involving (i) the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof; (ii) any structural component; (iii) the repair or replacement of any required component of a fire or smoke rated assembly; (iv) the alteration of any required means of egress system, including the addition or removal of emergency supplemental hardware; (v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.

permit.city_faq_quote: What is a building permit and when is one required? A Building Permit (BP) is a document that permits construction of or any change to the use of any property, as determined by the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (VUSBC), including additions and alterations [...] However, there are certain exemptions to requiring a building permit [...] If you are unsure if your project requires a building permit or if you have other questions contact the Permits and Inspections Division telephone at: (804) 646-4169 or by E-mail at: PDRPermitsandInspections@RVA.gov. [...] Zoning approval is required for most building permit applications, including interior renovations.
permit.note: The exempt list is the state's (Section 108.2 of the Virginia Construction Code, 13VAC5-63-80), which Richmond reproduces in its Commercial Building Plan Review Requirements guide (March 21, 2025). Neither the list nor Richmond's pages name toilet partitions or toilet compartments. Section 108.1 requires a permit for work 'involving the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof'; it does not say whether a toilet stall partition is a 'partition' in that sense, and the question is not decided here. Whether a like-for-like replacement is 'minor and ordinary' (items 13 and 14.11) is the building official's decision. The city's FAQ lists exemptions for 'common residential improvements' only.
permit.office: City of Richmond Bureau of Permits and Inspections, 900 E. Broad St., Room 108
permit.phone_quote: New Customer Service Line: Call 804-646-4169 to ask a question or to check on the status of a permit.

restrooms_city.note: No Richmond ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found: one web search returned nothing for the City of Richmond, and the city's permit pages, FAQ and commercial plan review guide say nothing about restroom signs. The Richmond City Code (Municode) could not be read, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'. Because the statewide building code supersedes local building regulations, the state rules in the state pack apply in Richmond as written.

public_wage.state_law_note: Virginia has a prevailing wage law (§ 2.2-4321.3): mandatory for state agencies on public works over $250,000, and for a locality only if it adopts an ordinance. Richmond has adopted one (see city_rule). The Department of Labor and Industry publishes no rate table; its page says determinations 'are based on the applicable prevailing wage rate determinations made by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the Davis-Bacon Act', and the statute says the state rate may 'in no event' be lower than the Davis-Bacon rate. So the federal determination for Richmond is the published figure, and the floor for a state determination.
public_wage.state_law_quote: "Prevailing wage rate" means the rate [...] as determined by the Commissioner on the basis of surveys conducted every three years, provided that (i) in no event shall the prevailing wage rate be lower than the prevailing wage rate determined by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the federal Davis-Bacon Act [...] C. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, any locality may adopt an ordinance requiring that, when letting contracts for public works paid for in whole or in part by funds of the locality [...] N. The provisions of this section shall not apply to any public contract for public works of $250,000 or less.
public_wage.city_rule: The City of Richmond has adopted a prevailing wage ordinance under Code of Virginia § 2.2-4321.3 C: Ordinance No. 2024-186, adopted October 15, 2024, in force July 1, 2025, adding Section 21-74 to the City Code. Each construction contract greater than $250,000 awarded by the City under Chapter 21 must require the contractor and subcontractors to pay at or above the prevailing wage rate as determined by the Virginia Commissioner of Labor and Industry. Contracts subject to federal prevailing wage law are exempt. Administered by the Department of Procurement Services, (804) 646-5716.
public_wage.city_rule_quote: Sec. 21-74. Payment of prevailing wage for work performed on certain construction contracts. (a) Each contract for construction greater than $250,000.00 awarded by the City pursuant to Chapter 21 shall require that the contractor and subcontractors pay wages, salaries, benefits, and other remuneration to any mechanic, laborer, or worker employed, retained, or otherwise hired to perform services in connection with the construction contract at or above the prevailing wage rate. (b) Certain contracts exempted. Construction contracts subject to Federal prevailing wage law are exempted from the City's prevailing wage requirement. [...] § 3. This ordinance shall be in force and effect on [January] July 1, 2025. [Cover:] ADOPTED: OCT 15 2024

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Richmond job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Virginia rules Richmond enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Richmond state office buildings, university halls, medical centers and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Virginia's statewide rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. A city can't change them, so Richmond enforces them as the state writes them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Richmond's Bureau of Permits and Inspections issues building permits. Virginia's statewide rules require a permit for work that adds or removes a wall or partition or changes the plumbing. They exempt replacing plumbing fixtures without touching the pipes, installing or replacing cabinetry or trim, and work the building official considers minor and ordinary. Richmond's guide for commercial projects repeats that list. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Bureau of Permits and Inspections (804-646-4169) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Richmond's Bureau of Permits and Inspections
page.install_rule: Virginia requires a state contractor license for commercial jobs over $1,000: Class C covers single jobs up to $30,000, Class B up to $150,000, and Class A $150,000 and above. Richmond confirms the license before it reviews a building permit application, and asks for a City of Richmond business license from a contractor whose work in the city came to $25,000 or more over the past 12 months. Confirm with the Bureau of Permits and Inspections and the Virginia Board for Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a job over $1,000, the contractor needs a Virginia contractor license, and a Richmond business license once its work in the city reaches $25,000 in 12 months.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state agency projects over $250,000, Virginia law requires at least the prevailing wage set by the state's Commissioner of Labor and Industry, and a city, county or school division has to pay it only if it has passed its own ordinance. Richmond passed one: since July 1, 2025, City of Richmond construction contracts over $250,000 carry the same requirement, unless federal wage rules already apply. The state bases its rates on the federal ones and may not set them lower. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in the City of Richmond is $21.10 an hour plus $1.11 in benefits. The city's Department of Procurement Services (804-646-5716) handles the rule on city contracts.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Richmond: 4.3% state, 1% city and a 0.7% regional tax that applies across Central Virginia.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices, courts and university buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel with heavy-duty hardware, for restrooms that serve the public all day.

The statewide code applies in every Virginia city without local amendments (see the state sources below). Checked 2026-11-24.

- When a permit is needed and what is exempt: [13VAC5-63-80, Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Section 108, Application for permit](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title13/agency5/chapter63/section80/) (Section 108.1, work that needs a permit; Section 108.2, exemptions), reproduced in Richmond's [Commercial Building Plan Review Requirements](https://www.rva.gov/sites/default/files/2025-03/Commercial%20Building%20Plan%20Submittal%20-%20March%202025.pdf) ("Building Permit Exemptions"), and the city's [Planning and Development Review FAQ](https://www.rva.gov/planning-development-review/faq) ("What is a building permit and when is one required?", phone 804-646-4169). None names toilet partitions. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Richmond: Virginia Tax, [Sales and Use Tax](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sales-and-use-tax) (6% in Central Virginia, Richmond City listed) and its [Sales Tax Rates by Locality](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/inline-files/sales-and-use-tax-rates-by-locality-by-date.xlsx) spreadsheet (Richmond City 6% since October 1, 2020); the regional 0.7% is in [Code of Virginia § 58.1-603.1](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/chapter6/section58.1-603.1/), subsection B; the other parts are in the sections listed under Sales tax below. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on City of Richmond contracts: City of Richmond Department of Procurement Services, [Prevailing Wage](https://www.rva.gov/procurement-services/prevailing-wage), and [Ordinance No. 2024-186](https://richmondva.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=6736412&GUID=E756F112-CF1E-4FBA-AB28-FC7C66697B97&Options=ID%7CText%7C&Search=2024-186), adopted October 15, 2024, in force July 1, 2025, adding Section 21-74 to the Code of the City of Richmond. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Carpenter rate on federally funded building work in the City of Richmond: [federal wage determination VA20260155, modification 2, October 15, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/VA20260155/2). State rates are based on the federal ones and may not be lower: [Code of Virginia § 2.2-4321.3](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title2.2/chapter43/section2.2-4321.3/) and [Virginia Department of Labor and Industry, Prevailing Wage Law](https://doli.virginia.gov/labor-law/prevailing-wage-law/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor license and business license checks before a permit: City of Richmond, [Commercial Building Plan Review Requirements](https://www.rva.gov/sites/default/files/2025-03/Commercial%20Building%20Plan%20Submittal%20-%20March%202025.pdf) ("Contractor's Licenses or Owner Statement") and the [Building Permit Application](https://www.rva.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/Building-PermitApplication_0.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by the 2021 Virginia Construction Code; 2021 Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Part I, Virginia Construction Code (2021 International Building Code with Virginia amendments, 13VAC5-63), in force since January 18, 2024, enforced in Richmond by the Bureau of Permits and Inspections of the Department of Planning and Development Review without local amendments (Code of Virginia § 36-98); 2021 Virginia Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Virginia amendments); Section 108 of the Virginia Construction Code (13VAC5-63-80) for permits; Section 21-74 of the Code of the City of Richmond (Ordinance No. 2024-186, in force July 1, 2025) for wages on city contracts; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Richmond building permit, and whether the building official reads 'the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof' to include toilet stall partitions (Bureau of Permits and Inspections, 804-646-4169, PDRPermitsAndInspections@rva.gov).

Richmond's prevailing wage page says '$250,000 or more' in its first line and 'greater than $250,000' below; the ordinance says 'greater than $250,000.00', and the page text follows the ordinance ('over $250,000').

The Richmond City Code (Municode) blocks automated access: Section 21-74 was read in the adopted ordinance on Legistar, not in the codified code, and the code was not checked for a restroom sign rule. A browser search of the code for 'restroom' and 'toilet' closes that.

Richmond's business license threshold is written from the city's commercial plan review guide ($25,000 or more of construction value in the city in the previous 12 months); the local-rules file words it as $25,000 a year in city revenue. The city's business license page (rva.gov/finance/business-license) returned 404.
The carpenter rate in the federal determination is a 2016 survey rate (SUVA2013-038) with $1.11 in benefits, and sits below the metro median wage shown in the bullet above it.
DHCD is working on the 2024 codes; older stakeholder memos found in a web search give a tentative October 2027 target. No effective date is fixed, so the page says nothing about it.
The four building types in the lead and the buyers bullet on state offices, courts and university buildings are editorial, not sourced.

The federal wage determination's class is 'Carpenter'; whether partition installers are classed as carpenters on a given job is the contracting agency's call. Whether Richmond Public Schools projects fall under the city ordinance was not checked.
